stem: Line \(\ell\) is shown in the \(xy\)-plane. Line \(m\) (not shown) has the same \(x\)-intercept as line \(\ell\), and the slope of line \(m\) is twice the slope of line \(\ell\). What is the \(y\)-coordinate of the \(y\)-intercept of line \(m\)?
solution: Line \(m\) has slope \(3\) and passes through \((-4, 0)\): \(y = 3(x + 4)\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. 6 is the \(y\)-intercept of line \(\ell\); doubling the slope from the same \(x\)-intercept doubles it.
explanation.B: Incorrect. 3 is the slope of line \(m\), not its \(y\)-intercept.
explanation.D: Correct. Line \(\ell\) has slope \(\frac{6}{4} = \frac{3}{2}\) and \(x\)-intercept \(-4\); line \(m\) is \(y = 3(x + 4)\), so its \(y\)-intercept is 12.

verify:
x = symbols('x')
p = figure['points']
ml = Rational(p[1]['y'] - p[0]['y'], p[1]['x'] - p[0]['x'])
xi = [q['x'] for q in p if q['y'] == 0][0]
b = (2*ml*(x - xi)).subs(x, 0)
assert b == 12
assert value(choices[answer]) == b
assert all(value(choices[k]) != b for k in choices if k != answer)
